messages:
sara: Hey - customer migrated org late last night. Console (Org dashboard) shows 1,500 trial credits but when they call the Billing API with their service key it returns available_credits = 0. Customer is @nina from ACME. Repro steps below, can someone triage?

nina: Confirmed — web UI shows the credits under the org header and in billing->credits, but our service key calls return 0. We need this fixed ASAP, prod feature gated by credits.

mike: Thanks. Can you paste the org_id and a masked service key (last 4)? Also which endpoint are they hitting?

sara: org_id: 67890, service_key: sk_live_***abcd
Endpoint they hit: `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/billing/usage` (we're calling the balance check before a job). Example request/response:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***abcd" -X GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/billing/credits
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "org_id": 67890,
  "available_credits": 0,
  "currency": "USD"
}```

mike: Hmm. Console pulling from master ledger shows credits. Two quick things: 1) Is this a project-level service key vs org-level key? 2) Any recent org->project remapping during migration?

nina: They used a project-scoped service key (created before migration). During migration projects were collapsed/renamed.

todd: Likely cause: project->org mapping mismatch post-migration. Console reads org-level aggregate ledger; project-scoped service key still points to old project id which has no credit allocation.

mike: Can you confirm the service key's linked project id? Run:`SELECT project_id FROM service_keys WHERE key_fingerprint='abcd'` — also check `SELECT sum(credits) FROM credit_allocations WHERE project_id = <that id>`

sara: Ran quick lookup, service key maps to project 55555; console shows credits allocated to org 67890 and project 99999 after migration.

billing-bot: [automated] Credit-resync job queued for org 67890 (job_id: resync-2026-03-17-0001). Estimated runtime: ~10 minutes.

mike: Good. Two remediation paths: 1) run resync (idempotent) so ledger allocations propagate to legacy service keys that map to the new projects via alias table, or 2) swap service key to an org-scoped key (quick workaround). I'd try resync first.

todd: Command we ran: `rdb-admin credits resync --org 67890 --force` — log tail:```
[00:01] lookup alias table for project mappings
[00:03] updated project 55555 -> canonical project 99999 (via alias)
[00:05] propagated 1500 credits to service key fingerprint abcd
[00:07] recomputed available_credits for service key sk_live_***abcd -> 1500
[00:07] completed resync job resync-2026-03-17-0001
```

nina: Re-tested. API now returns available_credits: 1500. UI and API match. Customer confirmed billing gating is unblocked.

mike: Root cause: migration created aliasing between old project IDs and new canonical projects but the periodic background resync didn't run/was skipped during the migration window. We should add a post-migration hook to trigger resync automatically.

sara: Filed follow-up ticket in #eng-infra: MIG-4321 — "post-migration credit resync hook". Noted to add telemetry to detect desyncs where console credits != service-key billing response.

todd: Also increased resync priority for orgs flagged as "migration_in_progress". Will monitor queue.

mike: Closing here since customer OK. If anyone finds additional accounts hit by this migration flow ping me. :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks all.
